A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Anny body model and Anny-One dataset. All text, equations, tables, figures, and end matter support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original scan-fitting experiments, HMR evaluations in Tables 1–3, and runtime and memory measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original scan-fitting and HMR results and adds empirical comparisons of shape distributions and cross-model representability.

M1.justification: Both versions use MakeHuman blendshapes, piecewise multilinear shape interpolation, skeletal posing, blend skinning, collision rejection, and sparse topology mappings. v3 expands implementation descriptions without establishing a change to these procedures or the HMR architectures.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on uniformly sampled synthetic Anny and SMPL-X shape populations, extending geometric testing beyond the retained real scans to model-generated morphologies, including extreme shapes. The named scan datasets, HMR benchmarks, and training-data sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Geometric validation gains direct SMPL-X scan-fitting comparisons and SMPL-X+A distribution comparisons; v2 primarily contextualized scan fitting using a cited ATLAS result. v3 Figure 7 labels the child comparator SMPL-X+A, although the prose says SMPL-X. The SMPL/SMPL-X runtime comparisons disappear. Comparator membership in HMR Tables 1–3 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New cross-model fitting uses 8,000 sampled meshes in each direction, a common SMPL-X topology, rest poses, and 300 SMPL-X coefficients within a two-standard-deviation-radius ball. The batch-size runtime/memory protocol is removed. Anny-One's reported size changes from 800k to 780k, without establishing retraining. Existing HMR splits, metrics, and configurations remain unchanged; v3 does not restate the child-scan hairnet exclusion.

E4.justification: v3 adds comparative weight–height distribution analysis, bidirectional shape-space fitting with error histograms, and benchmark-specific qualitative comparisons in Figure 9. These test population realism, representational coverage, and reconstruction behavior. Conversely, v2's runtime/memory scaling analysis is removed. The HMR ablations in Tables 1–2 remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, or significance tests. WHO 95% reference intervals already appear in v2 Figure 5. v3's new registration histograms describe variation across shapes, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Reported Anny–SMPL-X cyclic error changes from 3.2 to 1.3 mm, adult fitting error from 2.4 to 2.5 mm, and child fitting error from 2.7 to 2.0 mm. The child change cannot be treated as a verified same-protocol gain. v3 adds scan-baseline results, cross-fitting means of 3.2 and 5.0 mm, population statistics, and qualitative comparisons, while removing runtime/memory results. Every numerical entry in Tables 1–3 is retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the topology-regression formula from summing R_{j,i}v_j to R_{i,j}v_j, consistent with the stated M-by-N matrix mapping N source vertices to M targets. This repairs a dimensional indexing inconsistency; no new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the conclusion's state-of-the-art HMR claim to competitive performance, and Section 6.3 no longer claims consistent superiority across benchmarks. The main contributions—a scan-free, interpretable body model and a synthetic training dataset—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits conclusions from three child scans, acknowledges uncertainty about why Anny's parameterization helps HMR, and discusses SMPL-X's better skin-fold fitting alongside fitting of clothing and hair. It interprets cross-fitting failures as evidence of broader Anny shape coverage. The earlier discussion of Anny's runtime overhead is removed.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents 1,136 prototypical blendshapes, anatomical edits and skinning symmetry, fitting component counts, and identifiers for the three commercial child scans. These are additional disclosures, not established method changes. Runtime hardware and configuration details disappear with that study. The repository link and Apache 2.0 release information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to MHR, SMPL made Simple, global growth statistics, and 3DPeople, while removing the pose-space deformation reference. It describes ATLAS as concurrent work and briefly positions MHR relative to it. The broader positioning against scan-based body models remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and explanatory passages receive localized rewrites. Artist-designed models gain a separate related-work paragraph, Section 5 gains Adults/Children/Shape diversity subdivisions, the runtime section disappears, and acknowledgments are added. The main narrative sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout throughout. Shape illustrations are merged, calibration panels are reorganized and extended, scan-registration comparisons are redrawn, and new distribution histograms and benchmark qualitative panels appear. The runtime figure is removed, and tables and captions are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens geometric validation through direct scan-fitting baselines and tests of shape-space coverage. Its more restrained HMR claims better match unchanged Table 3, where Anny is not best on every metric. These gains outweigh, but are limited by, the loss of runtime/memory evidence and unresolved details surrounding the revised child-fitting results and comparator labeling.
